h: Pinchas Receives the Covenant of Life Through Self Sacrifice

p: in his being zealous with My zeal in their midst, etc.
הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת בְּרִיתִי שָׁלוֹם
Behold, I give him My covenant of peace."
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג רכ, א)
In the holy Zohar on this parshah (III 220a):
Say it with your own mouth,
for you hand it over to him, etc.;
מֹשֶׁה הֲוָה אָמַר הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ
Moshe was the one saying 'Behold, I give him';
for had it been the Holy One, blessed is He,
לָכֵן אֱמוֹר לוֹ הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן וְגוֹ׳
'Therefore say to him: Behold, I give, etc.';
but it is not written so,
And indeed the whole word "say" is superfluous,
דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לָכֵן הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן וְגוֹ׳
for it should have said, "Therefore, behold, I give, etc."
That is, the attribute of the tzaddik
בָּא עַל יְדֵי עֲטִיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
came through the counsel of the serpent,
עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁהִכְנִיס הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף לָאָדָם
through his bringing bodily pleasure into man,
that he feel his own pleasure.
And therefore Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
who was like Adam HaRishon before the corruption,
who did not feel bodily pleasure at all;
and then it was said of him (of Adam, Bereishis 2:25):
שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלָל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוּשָׁה בָּזֶה
for he did not know at all that there was shame in this.
And so Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
was like Adam HaRishon before the sin;
"What the lightest of the light would not say,
he said so only in order to bear offspring"
(as Rashi explained in parshas Vayeitzei, Bereishis 29:21,
that is, he knew nothing at all
and the feeling of his own pleasure,
(מִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם, זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלז, ב)
as is stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13):
Rather, he was from the inner side:
this one from the body, and this one from the soul";
וְהָיָה גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and he too was like Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
and furthermore he is from within.
וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים לֹא מֵת מֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵּי
"And some say Moshe did not die, etc.;
here too he stands and serves."
וְכֵן בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פט, א)
And so in the holy Zohar (II 89a):
וְלֹא יָדַע אִישׁ אֶת קְבוּרָתוֹ (דְּבָרִים לד, ו)
'And no man knows his burial place'" (Devarim 34:6);
that is, there is no grasp at all of this,
how the term burial can apply to him.
it is still written regarding Yaakov, outwardly,
But regarding Eliyahu, who is Pinchas
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י בָּבָא מְצִיעָא קיד, ב)
death is not written of him at all,
and this is what Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
וְהִנֵּה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
Now, Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, and Moshe Rabbeinu
in that they were born so,
like Adam HaRishon before the corruption;
the house was filled with light (Sotah 12a).
for he gave himself over for the sake of Yisrael
and did not fear the tribe of Shimon;
and this was through his concealing himself,
"He too has come in to fulfill his desires,"
And this is what it says:
"in his being zealous with My zeal in their midst":
through his being in their midst,
so that they mistook him to be one of them, etc.;
And this is what is said in the holy Zohar:
"You are the one who gave over your soul
and he turned back My wrath, etc.";
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה מְסִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁל פִּנְחָס
for this was the self-sacrifice of Pinchas,
he would not be executed for it.
That is why there is mentioned here
the name of the man who was struck,
which was not mentioned at the time of the incident:
to make known the self-sacrifice of Pinchas,
that the one struck was the prince of the tribe of Shimon;
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן זָכָה פִּנְחָס לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
and thereby Pinchas merited eternal life.
that he himself say "Behold, I give, etc.,"
for Moshe Rabbeinu is called "the man of God,"
from the Holy One, blessed is He, to His Shechinah;
וְאָמַר הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת בְּרִיתִי שָׁלוֹם
and he said, "Behold, I give him My covenant of peace."
And likewise Shabbos, which is the attribute of Malchus,
אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב צב, א)
is stated in the holy Zohar (II 92a)
to be "Shabbos in the secret of the covenant";
and when there are reckoned in the holy Zohar
the Mussaf of Shabbos is reckoned
are from the attribute of "the tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
and "those who taste it merit life,"
